exposure: Premature rupture of the fetal membrane (PROM) combined with subclinical chorioamnionitis
Premature rupture of the fetal membrane (PROM) without subclinical chorioamnionitis
cohort: The study included 80 pregnant patients with premature rupture of the fetal membrane (PROM), divided into an experimental group with subclinical chorioamnionitis and a control group without placental or fetal membrane lesions.
finding: Premature rupture of the fetal membrane combined with subclinical chorioamnionitis significantly worsened various pregnancy outcomes and was associated with reduced mRNA, protein expression, and serum concentrations of MMP-2.
mod_finding: The rate of cesarean section was significantly higher in patients with premature rupture of the fetal membrane combined with subclinical chorioamnionitis.
cross-section timing: Around the time of delivery, based on final placental pathological diagnosis results.
